summary: Implemented, via an Ansible playbook run from control_node node4, a policy that lets node2 (lan-a) reach node3 (lan-b) only on TCP/5432 while rejecting all other cross-LAN traffic, routed through node1 (VyOS). Also completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart/recovery verification for all four managed nodes.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1 (VyOS 2026.04 rolling, eth0=mgmt/dhcp, eth1=lan-a, eth2=lan-b, unconfigured), node2 (RHEL10, enp1s0=mgmt, enp8s0=lan-a, unaddressed), node3 (RHEL10, enp1s0=mgmt, enp8s0=lan-b, unaddressed), node4 (Ubuntu 24.04 ansible-controller, control_node)
Established passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user, via VyOS 'system login user vyos authentication public-keys') and to node2/node3 (root authorized_keys) using node4's existing keypair

Wrote /root/ansible/cross-lan-firewall/{inventory.ini,site.yml} on node4: nmcli-based static addressing for node2 (10.50.1.10/24) and node3 (10.50.2.10/24) with cross-subnet static routes via node1, a firewalld rich-rule on node3 scoping tcp/5432 inbound to source 10.50.1.0/24, and a VyOS shell task on node1 configuring eth1/eth2 addresses plus a zone-based firewall (zones LAN-A/LAN-B, rulesets LANA-TO-LANB allow tcp/5432 default-reject, LANB-TO-LANA allow established/related default-reject)

Discovered via VyOS conf_mode/firewall.py source that this rolling release requires 'firewall ipv4 name <ruleset>' (not 'firewall name'), 'firewall zone <z> member interface <if>' (not bare 'interface'), and valueless 'state established'/'state related' leaves; corrected the playbook accordingly and validated with commit+save

Ran the playbook to completion (idempotent on re-run) and functionally verified with real listeners/curl/ping: node2->node3:5432 succeeds, node2->node3:8000 and ICMP are rejected, node3->node2 initiated traffic is rejected

Diagnosed and fixed a false negative where node3's local firewalld (independent of VyOS) was rejecting the allowed 5432 traffic with 'admin prohibited', by adding a scoped rich-rule via ansible.posix.firewalld

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially: captured boot_id + service/config baselines, issued a background-delayed native reboot (VyOS: /sbin/reboot; Linux: systemctl reboot) so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to ~0, and re-verified interface/route/firewall config persistence and end-to-end policy behavior after each restart
Cleaned up all test HTTP listeners created for verification

evidence.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on TCP/5432
evidence.summary: curl from node2 to http://10.50.2.10:5432/ returns http_code=200 both before and after all node restarts

evidence.requirement: All other traffic between lan-a and lan-b is rejected
evidence.summary: node2->node3:8000 curl times out (000) and ping gets ICMP Destination Port Unreachable from the VyOS router; node3-initiated connection into node2 gets Connection refused, confirming default-reject in both firewall.ipv4 rulesets
Inventory and playbook authored on control_node node4; ansible-playbook syntax-check, ansible ping, and full/limited playbook runs all succeed and are idempotent on re-run

evidence.requirement: VyOS firewall/zone config correctness on node1
evidence.summary: conf_mode/firewall.py inspected to determine correct 2026.04 rolling syntax; commit succeeded with zones LAN-A/LAN-B, rulesets LANA-TO-LANB/LANB-TO-LANA, and show firewall/show firewall zone confirm active config with hit counters incrementing correctly
